h1: The 7 Best Air Purifiers Under $300 for Allergies, Pets and Smoke in 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Air Purifier Under $300: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 7 air purifiers for a budget under $300 from Coway, Blueair, Winix and Levoit, compared on room size, filters and smart control.
summary: The LEVOIT Core 400S-P is the air purifier to buy for most open living spaces, with app control and a stated 1,733 square foot rating at a mid-range price. The Coway Mighty AP-1512HH is the long-standing, low-fuss option with a 3-year warranty, the WINIX 5510 adds carbon for odour, and the Blueair 311i Max is the quiet large-room choice.
intro: The number printed on the box, a square-footage rating, is the most misleading figure in air purifiers. It describes how many square feet the unit can clean at a few air changes per hour under ideal conditions, often the ceiling for a single air change per hour. In a real living room with a couch, a pet and a window, you want a purifier rated for much more room than yours, because filtering is a function of flow, not just filter quality.

This ranking sorts seven purifiers by that idea, along with filter type, odour handling, smart features and running cost. Some are listed in the $100 to $200 bracket and some in the $200 to $500 bracket, so check the current price against your $300 limit before buying. We reviewed listings and spec sheets, and we did not measure air quality ourselves.

products.name: LEVOIT Smart Air Purifier for Home Large Room, Core 400S-P
products.verdict: App-connected large-room cleaning rated to 1,733 square feet at a mid-range price.
products.description:
The Core 400S-P is a tower purifier rated for up to 1,733 square feet, with app connectivity and a large-room design. Priced at $100 to $200, it is the best value among big-room smart models.

It ranks first because it combines wide coverage, app control and a price below the $200 mark in a single package. The coverage figure is the stated ceiling, and in a typical living room it gives you generous headroom to run on a lower, quieter fan speed. The compromise is that you buy replacement filters on a schedule, and the app, while handy, is optional.

Buy it if you have an open living area and want smart scheduling. Skip it if you want carbon-heavy odour control.
products.idealFor: Open living rooms where you want smart control.
products.skipIf: Cooking or smoke odours are your main concern.

products.name: COWAY Air Purifier for Home Up to 1,748ft2, Mighty AP-1512HH
products.verdict: Coway's best-known model, rated to 1,748 square feet, with auto and eco modes and a 3-year warranty.
products.description:
The Mighty AP-1512HH is rated for up to 1,748 square feet, has Auto and Eco modes with a filter indicator, and carries a 3-year warranty. It is listed in the $200 to $500 bracket, so verify the current price against your $300 limit.

It ranks second because it is the most established model in the category, with a long track record that makes replacement filters and owner advice easy to find. The auto mode adjusts fan speed to air quality, and the eco mode shuts the fan down when the air is clean. The warranty is the longest of the group. Against the Levoit above, it lacks app control.

Buy it if you want a reliable, proven purifier with a strong warranty. Skip it if you want app control.
pros: Long track record in the category
products.idealFor: Buyers who want a trusted, set-and-forget purifier.

products.name: WINIX 5510 Air Purifier (New Generation of 5500-2 with App Support) for Home Large Room
products.verdict: True HEPA plus a high-deodorization carbon filter and app support, rated to 1,881 square feet.
products.description:
The Winix 5510 is rated for up to 1,881 square feet, pairs a True HEPA filter with a high-deodorization carbon filter, adds app support and has an auto mode. It is the new generation of the 5500-2 and costs $100 to $200.

It takes third place because carbon filtration is what handles cooking smells, smoke and pet odours, which HEPA alone cannot do, and a purifier that tackles both is the right answer for many homes. The larger room rating is also useful. Against the Levoit, it offers a stronger odour stage but less brand ecosystem.

Buy it if odours matter as much as particles. Skip it if you want the biggest filter market.
products.idealFor: Kitchens, smokers and homes with strong smells.

products.name: BLUEAIR Blue Pure 311i Max Smart Air Purifier for Medium Rooms up to 2,107 Sq Ft
products.verdict: HEPASilent technology and a 2,107 square foot rating with WiFi and auto mode.
products.description:
The Blue Pure 311i Max is rated for up to 2,107 square feet, uses Blueair's HEPASilent technology, and adds WiFi and auto mode. It is listed in the $200 to $500 bracket, so confirm the price against your limit.

It ranks fourth because Blueair designs for quiet operation at high airflow, and the large rating means you can run it slowly. The cost is price and filter upkeep, and it is less obviously a bargain than the Levoit or Winix. The brand's design is a cylinder that stands in a corner and pulls air from the whole room.

Buy it if you want a quiet, smart purifier for a large room. Skip it if price is your first filter.
pros: Largest room rating in the group
products.idealFor: Large rooms where noise must stay low.

products.name: LEVOIT Smart Air Purifier for Home Pets Room, Vital 200S-P
products.verdict: Pet-focused filtration with app control, rated to 1,875 square feet.
products.description:
The Vital 200S-P is rated for up to 1,875 square feet, offers app connectivity and has pet-focused filtration. Priced at $100 to $200, it is the Levoit for homes with animals.

It ranks fifth because the Core 400S-P has a similar rating and a simpler purpose, so the Vital 200S-P is a niche pick. If you have a shedding pet, the pet-targeted filtration and the larger coverage are exactly what you want. If not, the Core is the better value.

Buy it if you share your home with a dog or cat. Skip it if you have no pets.
products.idealFor: Homes with shedding pets and open living areas.

products.name: Winix 9800 4-Stage True HEPA Air Purifier with WiFi and PlasmaWave, 500 Sq Ft
products.verdict: Four-stage filtration with PlasmaWave and WiFi, rated for 500 square feet.
products.description:
The Winix 9800 offers four-stage True HEPA filtration, PlasmaWave technology, WiFi connectivity and a 500 square foot rating. It sits in the $200 to $500 bracket, so check pricing.

It ranks sixth because the 500 square foot rating is much smaller than the rest of the group and the PlasmaWave layer is an ionization feature that some buyers prefer to switch off. It is better suited to a bedroom or office than a living room, and for that job it is fine. Compared with the Winix 5510, you get a smaller room rating for a higher price tier.

Buy it if you want PlasmaWave in a bedroom-sized purifier. Skip it if you want large-room coverage.
products.skipIf: You need to clean a large living room.

products.name: LEVOIT Air Purifier for Home Pets Bedroom Dorm Room, Washable Pre-Filter
products.verdict: A bedroom and dorm-sized pet purifier with a washable pre-filter that cuts replacement costs.
products.description:
This Levoit is sized for bedrooms and dorm rooms, has pet-focused filtration, and uses a washable pre-filter stage. Expect to pay $100 to $200.

Last place is earned since it is the smallest unit in the group and not designed for a living room. The washable pre-filter, though, catches pet hair and larger dust before it reaches the main filter, which extends filter life and lowers ongoing cost. For a single room, it is an easy-to-live-with unit.

Buy it if you need a compact purifier for a bedroom, dorm or small office. Skip it if you want whole-living-room coverage.
products.idealFor: Small bedrooms, dorms and pet corners.

methodology.title: Coverage and room fit
methodology.description: We compared stated square footage ratings, from 500 to 2,107 square feet, and rewarded generous headroom for real rooms.

methodology.title: Filtration stages
methodology.description: True HEPA, carbon, pre-filters and extras such as PlasmaWave were compared for particles and odours.

methodology.title: Controls and smart features
methodology.description: Auto mode, app support, WiFi, filter indicators and eco modes were weighed for daily convenience.

methodology.title: Warranty and running cost
methodology.description: Warranty length and washable pre-filters were treated as indicators of ownership cost.

methodology.title: Price against the $300 limit
methodology.description: Each unit's price bracket was checked against the cap, and units in the $200 to $500 bracket are flagged for price verification.

whatMatters.detail: A square footage rating assumes a fixed number of air changes per hour, usually fewer than you want for allergies. If you want about five air changes per hour, pick a purifier rated for roughly twice your room. Compare your room's size to the stated rating, and leave headroom.
True HEPA captures 99.97 percent of particles at 0.3 microns under test, which includes pollen, dust and pet dander. Be wary of HEPA-type or HEPA-like wording. The listing should say True HEPA.
HEPA does not remove gases or smells. Activated carbon does, and a heavier carbon layer is more effective for smoke, cooking and pet odours. Check the listing for a carbon or deodorization filter.

whatMatters.factor: Noise at the speed you use
whatMatters.detail: A purifier that is quiet at the lowest speed but loud at the highest is typical. The quiet speed is where you will live, so a big room rating helps you stay there. Check the noise range on the listing.

The purchase price is only part of the cost. Filters need replacing every six to twelve months in most models, so check the price and availability. Washable pre-filters stretch the main filter's life.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: True HEPA, a room rating well above your room, and a filter indicator. Run it continuously rather than only when symptoms flare.

cards.label: In this ranking
cards.text: The Levoit Core 400S-P and Coway Mighty AP-1512HH are the best allergy picks, and the Winix 5510 adds carbon for odours.

cards.text: You want a very large room covered quietly. The Blueair 311i Max and Coway Mighty AP-1512HH justify a higher price.

faq.q: Do air purifiers work for allergies?
faq.a: They can reduce airborne allergens like pollen, dust and pet dander when a True HEPA filter is sized correctly for the room. They do not replace cleaning, or medical advice from your doctor.

faq.q: What is the common mistake when buying one?
faq.a: Buying a unit rated for the exact size of your room. Choose one rated well above your square footage, and run it continuously at a low speed.

faq.q: Is the Coway Mighty worth it over the Levoit Core 400S-P?
faq.a: If you want a long warranty and an established model, yes. If you want app control and a lower price, the Levoit is the better buy.
Remove the plastic wrapping from the filters, install them, plug in the unit and press power. App models need a few extra minutes to pair.

faq.q: How often do I change filters?
faq.a: Most makers suggest every six to twelve months, depending on air quality and use. Filter indicator lights, like on the Coway, prompt you.
Ionizing features can produce small amounts of ozone in some designs. Many buyers choose to turn them off, so check the maker's guidance.

finalTake: For most homes, the LEVOIT Core 400S-P is the best air purifier under $300 because it combines large-room coverage, app control and a mid-range price. The Coway Mighty AP-1512HH is the proven alternative with a 3-year warranty, and the WINIX 5510 is the one to buy when odours matter. Always check the current price against your limit, and choose a unit rated for more than your room.
